seoTitle: Free SQL DDL to Django Models Converter (models.py)
metaDescription: Convert CREATE TABLE statements to Django models with field types, null/blank, unique, defaults and ForeignKey. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Converts CREATE TABLE statements into Django models.py code with max_length, decimal precision, null and blank, unique, defaults, ForeignKey and db_table so the models map onto the existing tables.
why: Django ships with inspectdb, but it needs a configured project and a live database. When you only have SQL, for example a dump from a legacy system, you must write the models yourself. This tool generates them from the DDL: the right field class for each column, max_length for varchar, decimal precision, null and blank, unique, defaults and ForeignKey with on_delete. It sets db_table and db_column so the models point at the existing tables instead of creating new ones. The implicit id AutoField is left out, and composite primary keys become unique_together because Django has no composite keys. Review and set managed = False if the tables are not yours to migrate. It runs in your browser.
howTo: Paste your CREATE TABLE statements into the input box.
Run the conversion to get the model classes.
Copy them into models.py, check field types and on_delete choices, and decide whether the models should be managed by Django.

faq.q: Why is the id field missing?
faq.a: Django adds an implicit auto-incrementing id, so a simple integer primary key called id is omitted. Other primary keys are written explicitly.

faq.q: How are composite primary keys handled?
faq.a: Django does not support them, so the columns become a unique_together constraint. You may need to designate one field as the primary key by hand.

faq.q: Will the models match my existing tables?
faq.a: They use db_table and db_column, so yes in naming. Set managed = False in Meta if migrations should not touch the tables.
As ForeignKey fields with an on_delete value chosen from the DDL. Check the target model and on_delete behaviour against your intent.
